chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged regarding the flood of the valley of Mahzour that the upper part should withhold the water upon the lower part for the palm trees up to the two ankles, and for the crops up to the two shoe straps. Then the water should be sent to the lower part from that for the crops to the shoe strap, and for the palm trees to the ankle. Then the water should be sent to the lower part from that.
Ibn Abi Umeyr said: And Mahzour is a place of the valley.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on water distribution between upper and lower landowners in a valley?
ai.summary: This hadith, cited in *Al-Kafi*, records the Prophet’s judicial ruling (*qada*) in the valley of Mahzour, establishing a precise hydraulic hierarchy where upper landowners retain water to a specific depth (ankle-deep for palms, shoe-strap-deep for crops) before releasing it downstream. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle of preventing water hoarding (*kaf al-ma'*) and ensuring equitable distribution, serving as a foundational precedent for Islamic water rights jurisprudence (*fiqh al-miya*).
